core_obligations: Show that the single morphism from the disjoint union of the members of the standard covering is again a covering in the topology (statement lines 2918-2919, used at proof lines 2943-2944).
Record that the standard covering refines the covering given by the disjoint union (statement lines 2920).

Compute the p-fold fibre products: the p-fold fibre product over U of the disjoint union is the disjoint union over all p-tuples of the p-fold fibre products over U of the members (proof lines 2934-2942).

Use that a sheaf takes disjoint unions to products, which applies because disjoint unions are coverings in the topology, to identify the degree p terms of the two Cech complexes compatibly with the differentials, giving the asserted isomorphism of complexes (proof lines 2942-2944).
proof_roadmap: Identify the fibre products of the coproduct with coproducts of fibre products (proof lines 2934-2942).
Apply the sheaf condition on disjoint unions (proof lines 2942-2944).
Read off that the comparison map of Cech complexes is an isomorphism (statement lines 2921-2929).
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares two coverings of an affine object U of a site of the form given by the big site for one of five topologies, or the small etale site, or the small Zariski site: a standard affine covering by finitely many morphisms, and the single morphism from their disjoint union; it asserts that the latter is a covering, that the former refines it, and that the induced map between the associated Cech complexes is an isomorphism of complexes (statement lines 2903-2931). The proof is short but it is an explicit computation: the p-fold fibre product of the disjoint union with itself over U is identified with the disjoint union over all p-tuples of indices of the corresponding p-fold fibre products of the members, and then the sheaf condition on disjoint unions, which holds because a disjoint union is itself a covering in the topology, identifies the degree p term of one Cech complex with that of the other in a way compatible with the differentials (proof lines 2933-2944). The claim is H2: the identity on fibre products of coproducts is the whole content, and it has to be written down and then combined with the sheaf axiom to see that the map of complexes is an isomorphism.
